title: Listening Part 1: Surviving Self-Corrections & Spelled Details
strategy_steps: During the 30-second preview before audio starts, underline the word/number limit and predict the exact category for every gap (surname, postcode, date, fee, noun).
Stay alert for speaker self-corrections triggered by 'oh wait', 'actually', 'sorry I meant', or 'that was last year's rate'.
Write down spelled names and postcodes immediately letter-by-letter; watch out for double letters ('double R') and lookalike letters (G/J, B/P, A/E/I).
Verify plurals and exact spelling before moving on — missing a final '-s' costs the mark.
common_mistakes: Writing down the first date, price, or room mentioned and stopping active listening before the speaker corrects themselves.
Exceeding ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER by writing redundant units or articles already printed beside the blank.
Dropping plural '-s' endings when the surrounding grammar requires a plural noun.
band_upgrade_patterns: Band 6 -> Band 8: Treat the first number or option spoken in Part 1 as a provisional draft until the conversation clearly moves to the next bullet point.

title: Map & Floorplan Labelling: Anchoring Orientation Before Audio Starts
strategy_steps: Locate the 'You Are Here' / Main Entrance point and compass directions (North/South/East/West) before the recording begins.
Trace every labelled landmark already printed on the map (e.g., courtyard, café, staircase) — the speaker always navigates relative to those anchors.
Follow the speaker's path physically with your eyes/cursor as they say 'turn left past...', 'directly opposite...', 'in the far corner...'.
Notice when the speaker resets back to the entrance ('Coming back to the foyer...') for the next question.
common_mistakes: Losing left/right orientation halfway through a gallery or park tour.
Confusing 'adjacent to' (next to) with 'opposite' (facing across a corridor or lawn).
Panicking after missing one label and falling behind on the next three locations.
band_upgrade_patterns: Band 6 -> Band 8: Mentally map prepositions of place ('just beyond', 'tucked behind', 'flanking the entrance') before pressing Play.

title: Listening Parts 2 & 3 Multiple Choice: Defeating Distractor Mentions
strategy_steps: Read the question stem carefully during prep time and underline the exact focus (e.g., 'What do BOTH students agree on?' vs 'Why did Maya change her mind?').
Expect ALL three options (A, B, C) to be mentioned in the audio — two will be rejected, qualified, or belonged to the past.
Listen closely to agreement/disagreement markers ('I used to think that, though...', 'Fair point, let's stick with...', 'That sounds expensive').
Match synonyms rather than exact words from the option list.
common_mistakes: Picking the first option whose exact keyword is spoken aloud (classic IELTS word-bait distractor).
Ignoring speaker attribution in Part 3 when one student suggests an idea and the tutor or partner rejects it.
band_upgrade_patterns: Band 6 -> Band 8: Track each option as 'Mentioned -> Confirmed or Rejected?' instead of locking in early.

title: Listening Part 3 Matching & Part 4 Lecture Signposting
strategy_steps: Remember that the numbered questions (e.g. 26–30) always occur IN ORDER in the recording, while the lettered box options (A–F) are paraphrases.
Listen for topic transition signposts ('Moving on to...', 'Next, regarding...', 'Finally, let's look at...') to stay synchronized with the numbered list.
Focus on the speaker's final verdict or evaluation after discussing pros and cons.
common_mistakes: Waiting to hear the exact words printed in options A–F instead of listening for paraphrased meanings.
Losing track of which numbered item is currently being discussed in a fast academic dialogue.
band_upgrade_patterns: Band 6 -> Band 8: Paraphrase each short option in the box mentally during prep time (e.g., 'lacks statistical reliability' -> 'too small a sample').
